checks: Pairing a new left point with a facet-supporting point at base 1 and taking the strictly weighted base-0 combination proves each facet inequality of T for the left point. Reflection gives the right side.

For the one-positive-vertex side of any through-centroid cut, (1+s)(1+t)=2+st with s+t=1 lies in [2,9/4], and equality at 9/4 requires equal negative values. The complementary side has fraction at least 1/2. This gives exactly the three active rays, including exclusion of the zero-vertex boundary case.

A strictly interior containing halfspace can be tightened through the centroid with strict own mass loss. A pure-base cap pays the entire own fiber. The exposed-site identity fixes the old raw minimum at 4|T|/9, so any actual active cap has zero other-fiber area.
At base zero, zero other-fiber area forces a≤−2/3. The barycentric margin is at least −1/3 on T, so any integer base z≤−1 gives strict margin ≥1/3. Reflecting the base treats the other source.
The two side probabilities sum to one and lower-bound their respective menu scores for every cap mixture. The old depth fraction divides 4|T|/9 by 2|T|.

dependencies.hypotheses: At both old sampled endpoints the positive base is strictly exposed and T is a full-dimensional simplex, so its intrinsic ordinary centroid maximum is 4|T|/9 and equals its mixed depth.

overlap.comparison: This establishes ordinary depth and the original extremal product value. It does not give the all-tilt strict margin on preserving extrapolated fibers, which is the new conclusion.

readability: The scores are for ordinary caps only. The source has a separate positive-width obstruction outside this draft.
summary: Every ordinary active cap on the corresponding side captures every preserving birth point, with the claimed strict margin.
